newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to delay airport trial of bag matching.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to delay airport trial of bag matching.

text.p: The White House aviation safety panel and airlines have decided to postpone a trial of bag matching to passengers at a hub airport -- originally due next month -- in order to test potential disruptive effects.
The decision was announced on Friday by a senior official of the Air Transport Association, the trade group of major U.S. carriers.
John Meenan, ATA vice president for policy and planning, said both sides agreed after a meeting to run computer tests on bag matching before the procedure was put into action at a major airport.
The Aviation Safety and Security commission, headed by Vice President Al Gore, recommended on Sept. 9 that at least one hub airport try a full bag match within 60 days.

But airlines protested that an untested trial -- to assure that someone did not check in a bag with a bomb and then not board the plane -- would create massive disruptions at both the test airport and connecting airports.
An administration official described the decision to run computer tests as an "improvement."
But he said starting tests at a few airports would not be representative of how bag matching might work nationally.

Meenan said the computer testing would include determining the number of bags that might have to be pulled from a flight, the time to take bags off the plane, inspecting them and then returning the matched bags.
Meenan of the ATA warned that implementing a full bag match now would cause aviation to grind to a near halt -- "bags would be lined up on runways ... Thousands of passengers delayed."
He added: "We don't believe that is what the commission desired."

Some industry officials have questioned bag matching for domestic travel, saying it could cause massive airport snarls and require costly airport expansions to handle the thousands of passengers required to wait for bags to be matched.
The commission was formed by President Bill Clinton after the July 17 crash of Trans World Airlines Flight 800 off Long Island, killing all 230 people on board.
